sn42.10:1.1: A century after the Buddha, the use of money by the mendicants of Vesālī precipitated a crisis in the Saṅgha. This led to the Second Council, at which the prohibition was reaffirmed. The current discourse is one of several cited against the use of money ([pli-tv-kd22:1.4.1]()).
sn42.10:1.3: Literally “gold and silver” (_jātarūparajata_), but _rajata_ is explained in [pli-tv-bu-vb-np18:2.8]() as currency made from any material.
sn42.10:2.1: Despite his impressive name (“Jeweled Crest”), this chief does not appear elsewhere.
sn42.10:3.6: This principle is still followed today. Mendicants generally should not ask for things. But they may ask for necessities from appropriate people, such as monastery attendants, people who have offered an invitation, or relatives.
